rationale:
bugs_open/367. `required-fields-missing-handler` is a triage ROUTER: it repairs nothing, it runs one SQL classification per `required_fields_missing` item and then converts, parks or closes it. To classify it must first FIND the component the finding names, and it looked with `WHERE pc.build_status = 'deployed'`. When that resolved nothing the routing CASE fell to `stale`, and `stale` CLOSES the item: status='complete', no error, one attempt, evidence 'page or deployed component no longer exists'.

That was coherent while the type had ONE producer. Seed 410 (bugs_closed/277) deliberately mirrored that producer's own filter — `check_required_fields_missing.go` is a POST-DEPLOY check and scans deployed rows — so `stale` meant 'my producer's predicate no longer matches'. bugs_closed/342 then added a SECOND producer at render time (work_items_common.go:562, live v1.0.1330) whose ENTIRE STATED PURPOSE is reaching the population the post-deploy check cannot see. Its findings are by construction about components that are not deployed. The router closes them as gone.

Confirmed live 2026-08-23 by reading the classify SQL out of this agent's own row and running it with its two params bound, for item 562788c3: route=stale, component_id='', html_len=0 — while the component sat there, 0a1498b3 on page f438eca6, slot 'tool-cta', build_status='pending', UNLOCKED, 9,220 chars of rendered_html, and the finding was TRUE (headline and trust_note genuinely empty, n_still_empty 2 of 2).

THE HARM IS THE SILENCE. Pre-342 these items failed three times and parked: ugly and legible. Now a true finding is recorded `complete` with no error, so any census asking 'did we action our required-fields findings?' scores it a success.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY 'WIDEN THE FILTER', which is what the bug file's own candidate 1 proposed and what I started from. Two measured reasons made me narrow it:
(1) The repair arm would hard-fail. `partial` converts via `file_rewrite`, which reads spec.component_id, .page_id, .component_function and .reason. The post-deploy producer writes all four (62 of 62 items carry component_id and page_id, 2026-08-23); the render-time producer writes NONE (0 of 3). An unresolved spec_paths entry and an unresolved item_key_suffix_field are both deliberate HARD ERRORS (create_work_item_action.go:281,294 and :252-256). So widening alone routes correctly and then dies one step later — a loud failure replacing a silent one, but still no repair.
(2) The repair arm is the wrong place for this population anyway. content_rewrite/edit_live runs at page-build-handler, whose save step DELETEs every agent-writable row on the page and reinserts at 'deployed' (save_page_sections_action.go:823, :1014). 28 of 31 `from_rfm` conversions were ALREADY failing at exactly that step on the owned-page refusal as of 2026-08-23 — that is bugs_open/333, filed 2026-08-19, OWNED by the 277 lane — and the 367 page is itself rebuild_policy=owned. Separately 'pending'/'needs_rebuild' are mid-flight states fix_component_template_action.go:843 refuses to touch on purpose, and the 17 'approved' rows are verbatim-adopted pages whose content_data is a provenance envelope (adopt_verbatim.go:514).

SO THE RULE INSTALLED IS NARROWER AND STRONGER THAN 'WIDEN': a disposer may close only on POSITIVE EVIDENCE of absence; a failed lookup is not evidence, and neither is a non-deployed target. The estate already rules this way one door over — revalidate_review_queue_action.go:684 on the same class of miss: 'That MIGHT mean the finding is moot, but it might equally be a lookup miss — so it is not positive evidence and the item stays queued.' The router now obeys the same rule: `stale` requires page-gone, or locked (277's accept-as-is), or a 'removed' row actually sitting at the slot; everything else PARKS at needs_human_review holding its dedup key, as the router's four existing park arms do.

CONSUMERS NAMED AND TOLD (2026-07-29 ruling section 3). bugs_open/333's lane: this change does NOT add load to their dead end — it keeps the non-deployed population out of page-build-handler entirely — and I am contributing the 31-item from_rfm census into their file. The review-queue revalidator's owners: its own lookup (loadPageComponentBySlotRO) has no build_status filter at all, so this change moves the router TOWARDS the revalidator's scope, not away. The tool lanes: nothing changes for deployed components.

WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, so nobody thinks it was missed: it does not make the population repairable (that needs 333 plus a producer that writes the convert arm's read-set — both named, neither taken); it does not re-key file_rewrite to triage.component_id (mechanically possible but it re-opens a council-settled key design in CQ-023 and buys nothing once the population parks); it does not register a verifier for this item_type (CQ-023 already warns one would fail-close this router's own `converted` arm); and it does not touch the 19 hand-typed `pc.build_status = 'deployed'` reads elsewhere, which are all PRODUCERS whose failure mode is under-detection — only a disposer turns non-detection into an affirmative claim of absence.

ONE EDIT IS IN THE COMMIT BUT NOT IN THIS PLAN, named so it is not a hidden change. Seed 410 gets a comment-only header pointer saying 574 supersedes its comp predicate, its stale arm and both close-arm evidence strings, and that re-applying 410 alone reverts them. It is comment-only, so 097 refuses it as an edit ('a fix plan proposes changes, not observations') and it is correct to — there is nothing there for a reviewer to judge. The residual it mitigates is real and only partly closed: 410 is an ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE whole-config seed and its verify block asserts branch wiring and park statuses but never the resolution predicate, so a hand re-run would silently revert this and still pass its own checks. Making 410 self-guard was considered and rejected: an assertion that the NEW predicate is present would make 410 abort on every re-run, which breaks it as a from-scratch seed. The honest fix belongs to whoever next touches 410 — assert the predicate it itself writes.

plan.summary: Make the required_fields_missing router stop disposing of findings it could not resolve. One config-only migration: resolve components on the lifecycle axis (not 'removed') rather than the build axis (= 'deployed'); require positive evidence for the `stale` close; add a fifth PARK route for a target that is real but not dispatchable; expose a target_state column so the cause is legible in orchestration_states; and correct two close-arm evidence strings that are false as written.

edits.symbol: classify.config.query — comp CTE + tomb CTE + routing CASE + target_state output
edits.rationale: Surgical replace() on five verbatim anchors, each asserted to occur EXACTLY ONCE in the LIVE row before any write (not in the seed file — 410 was edited in place three times and the live row is version=1). Aborts if an anchor has moved, if the two close-arm evidence strings are not the text this was written against (another lane got there first), if already applied, or if the rewrite is a no-op. snapshot_agent first. The COALESCE in the new predicate is load-bearing: NULL passes the 049 CHECK and a bare <> is NULL-unsafe, which would silently drop such a row — the wrong fail direction for something that closes items. Spelled to match the estate's one existing named rendering of this judgement, pageComponentNotRemovedSQL (section_editor_actions.go:1537).

edits.symbol: new steps route_not_dispatchable + park_not_dispatchable, spliced into the else-cascade
edits.rationale: A fifth PARK, not a fifth close. Inserted after route_resolved's else arm and ahead of route_owned, so the non-dispatchable case is decided BEFORE any repair arm can claim it. Parking at needs_human_review holds the dedup key, which is 410's whole anti-churn design; a close would release it and let the producer re-raise into the same wrong disposition. The error_message names the measured reason no automated repair is offered, so the human reading the row does not have to rediscover it.

edits.rationale: Both are false as written. close_stale asserts the component 'no longer exists' — row-absence cannot support a claim about history when 336 of 2,160 slots named in pages.sections ordinarily have NO page_components row at all (measured 2026-08-23). close_resolved says 'the currently-deployed component', which the widened resolution falsifies. The new close_stale text also points the reader at triage.target_state rather than at the row, because the dispatch loop's mark_complete OVERWRITES site_work_items.result on completed rows (277's RUNBOOK:60) — so orchestration_states is the only durable record of a close's cause, and prose on the close arm cannot be the audit trail.
edits.sketch:
jsonb_set(default_config, '{workflow,steps,close_stale,config,result_fields,evidence}', to_jsonb(
  'CLOSED ON POSITIVE EVIDENCE, one of three: the page row is gone; or the component at (page_name, slot_name) '
  'is LOCKED, which bugs_closed/277 treats as the deliberate accept-as-is resolution; or nothing resolves there '
  'and a build_status=''removed'' row is sitting at that slot. Which leg fired is triage.target_state in the '
  'orchestration record — read it there, because mark_complete overwrites this row''s result at completion. A '
  'lookup that simply finds nothing is NOT one of these and no longer closes anything (bugs_open/367): 336 of '
  '2,160 slots named in pages.sections had no page_components row at all on 2026-08-23, so absence of a row was '
  'never evidence that one existed. The dedup key releases; discovery rotation re-raises within days if the '
  'finding is still real.'::text), false)

edits.rationale: A block of bare SELECTs cannot gate a COMMIT — ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set (RFC_006's trap) — so every assertion RAISEs. Includes NEGATIVE CONTROLS: a botched replace() that ate a CTE would still satisfy 'the new predicate is present', so the block also requires plan_src, has_open_tool_recreation, n_asset_empty and no_plan_unbuildable to survive. Re-asserts 410's own invariants because this migration rewires one of its arms: all 18 branch arms by name, all FIVE park arms at needs_human_review (the new one included — a close there would be this very defect wearing a new name), classify still takes exactly 2 params, and step count 20 -> 22.

Reverses the five query edits on the same verbatim anchors, deletes the two added steps, re-joins route_resolved.else_step to route_owned, and restores both evidence strings. Asserts the reverse was TOTAL (no trace of target_not_dispatchable/target_state/tomb/bs survives and the old predicate is back) before committing, because a partial reverse leaves a cascade pointing at a step that no longer exists. Its header states plainly that rolling back REINSTATES a silent defect, and offers the safer partial: disarm the new route and keep the honest resolution and evidence. PROVEN: apply-then-rollback in one transaction returns default_config BYTE-IDENTICAL.

grounded_in: LIVE classify SQL, read from agent_definitions and run by hand with both params bound, item 562788c3, 2026-08-23: route=stale, component_id='', html_len=0 — while component 0a1498b3 at that (page, slot) is build_status='pending', UNLOCKED, 9,220 chars of rendered_html, and the finding is true (n_still_empty 2 of n_named 2).

WHOLE-POPULATION re-classification, all 65 required_fields_missing items ever filed, old query vs new, in one plpgsql loop: EXACTLY ONE route changes. Unchanged: partial 28, no_content_data 21, resolved 11, malformed 2, no_plan_owned 1, no_plan_unbuildable 1. Disconfirmable — 17 (page_id, slot_name) pairs carry >1 non-removed row and 0 of them switch which row ORDER BY pc.updated_at DESC LIMIT 1 picks.

POSITIVE CONTROLS, run against the PATCHED row inside a transaction that was then rolled back: a slot whose only row is build_status='removed' (tool-clip-path/ported-page) STILL routes stale with target_state='component_retired'; a page that does not exist STILL routes stale with target_state='page_missing'. The real item routes target_not_dispatchable with target_state='pending' and the component RESOLVES. A fix that satisfied only the last of these would have disabled a real close route.
'removed' is a LIVE, growing terminal, not dead history: 36 of 38 rows written in August 2026, most recent 2026-08-23 12:59Z — so the retirement control had something to bite on.

create_work_item_action.go:281 'spec_paths: a configured path that does not resolve is a HARD ERROR' and :252-256 'item_key_suffix_field: path %q did not resolve; refusing to fall back to the site-wide key %q, which is the collision this field prevents'. Producer spec shapes measured 2026-08-23: post-deploy 62 of 62 carry component_id and page_id; render-time 0 of 3. So widening ALONE routes correctly and dies at the next step.

save_page_sections_action.go:823 DELETEs every agent-writable row on the page and :1014 reinserts at 'deployed'. 28 of 31 content_rewrite:from_rfm conversions are ALREADY failed at that step on the owned-page refusal (2026-08-23) — bugs_open/333, filed 2026-08-19, owned by the 277 lane — and the 367 page is rebuild_policy=owned.

revalidate_review_queue_action.go:684, the estate's existing ruling on this exact class of miss: 'That MIGHT mean the finding is moot, but it might equally be a lookup miss — so it is not positive evidence and the item stays queued.'

336 of 2,160 slots named in pages.sections on non-deleted pages have NO page_components row at all (2026-08-23; vocabulary-checked — 1,824 of 2,160 DO resolve, and sampled pages show sections entries and slot_name values are the same vocabulary). So close_stale's 'no longer exists' is false across an ordinary population, quite apart from the build_status narrowing.

idx_swi_dedup is UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) WHERE status <> ALL (complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled) — so a close RELEASES the dedup key and a park HOLDS it. That is why the residue must park rather than close: a close lets the producer re-raise into the same wrong disposition.
plan.risks:
RISK 1 — the population parks rather than being repaired. Deliberate and stated: no safe automated repair exists for a non-deployed target today (see the save_page_sections DELETE, bugs_open/333's 28 measured refusals, and the mid-flight pending/needs_rebuild states). Parking at needs_human_review with the facts on the row MEETS 277's own stated bar — 'no item of this type ever again sits unread without a classification' — and is exactly what the bug file's own candidate 2 asked for. It does not meet 'every repairable one is dispatched', because this population is not currently repairable; that is named, not hidden.

RISK 2 — widening resolution means resolved/no_content_data/asset_sourced can now fire on a non-deployed row. Measured across all 65 live items: none do today. It is also the direction the review-queue revalidator already takes — loadPageComponentBySlotRO has NO build_status filter at all — so this moves the two closers closer together, not further apart.

RISK 3 — the new route is an eighth-plus route on an already branchy cascade, and RFC_030 tracks router proliferation. This adds no NEW router; it adds one arm to an existing one, and the verify block asserts all 18 branch arms by name so a mis-wire cannot ship.

RISK 4 — a hand re-run of seed 410 would revert this. Mitigated by the comment-only header pointer in edit 6. Not fully mitigated: 410's verify block still cannot detect the reversion. The honest fix is for 410 to assert its own predicate, which belongs to whoever next touches that file.

RISK 5 — 'removed' is written by only one registered Go path (page_admin_handlers.go:576, which also locks what it removes) plus hand-run SQL, and the dominant retirement verb is actually row DELETION by save_page_sections. So the component_retired leg is narrower than it looks, and a deleted row reads as lookup_miss and PARKS rather than closing. That is the safe direction and it is intentional, but it means some genuinely-gone components will park for a human instead of closing themselves. Watch the parked count at +7 days.

NOT A RISK, checked: apply-then-rollback in one transaction returns default_config BYTE-IDENTICAL, and the migration's own verify block plus all three behavioural controls were run against the patched row in a transaction that was then rolled back — nothing was applied to production to test this.
